text: About 3,600 years ago, warrior chiefs in mainland Greece grew rich from war, raiding and trade.
At Mycenae they were buried in deep graves with gold masks, gold cups and bronze swords.
src: From about 1600 BCE warrior chiefs on the Greek mainland grew rich / These burials reveal a warrior elite enriched by war, raiding and trade
At Mycenae two circles of deep shaft graves ... held men, women and children buried with gold masks, diadems and cups, bronze swords

text: Later, kings ruled from palaces, like the one at Pylos called the Palace of Nestor.
Most people lived in villages, growing wheat, barley, olives and grapevines and keeping sheep and goats.
src: by 1400 BCE kings ruled palace states at Mycenae, Pylos, Thebes and elsewhere / The best-documented kingdom is Pylos in Messenia, whose palace ... is called the Palace of Nestor
Most people lived in villages, growing wheat, barley, olives and vines and keeping sheep and goats

text: Their scribes wrote on clay tablets in Linear B, the oldest known written Greek.
The tablets name gods such as Zeus, Hera and Poseidon.
src: Scribes wrote on clay tablets / the Linear B tablets, the oldest written Greek
They name many gods who were still worshipped a thousand years later: Zeus and Hera; Poseidon

text: Their craftsmen made fine things of gold, silver and ivory, like this gold mask from Mycenae.
src: Craftsmen excelled in small works: the gold cups from Vapheio ... bronze daggers inlaid with gold and silver; carved ivory / buried with gold masks

text: They traded across the Mediterranean, sending painted jars of wine and perfumed oil as far as Egypt.
In return came copper, tin, gold, ivory, glass and amber.
src: The Mycenaeans traded across the Mediterranean. Their painted pottery, much of it containers for wine and perfumed oil, is found from Sardinia ... to Cyprus, the Levant and Egypt
In return came copper from Cyprus, tin, gold, ivory, glass and Baltic amber

text: About 3,200 years ago, their palaces were destroyed and writing was forgotten.
Centuries later, the poet Homer remembered Mycenae as a city “rich in gold”.
src: Around 1200 BCE the palaces were destroyed and writing was forgotten
Homer’s Iliad and Odyssey, composed probably in the 8th or 7th century BCE ... remember Mycenae “rich in gold” / Around 1250 BCE its walls were extended and the Lion Gate built
